heroHeadline: Trump Declares Russia-Ukraine Ceasefire Talks 'Immediately' as Russia Fires Record 6,804 Weapons in April
heroSubtitle: Following a 90-minute Trump-Putin call, Trump told reporters on May 1 that Russia and Ukraine will begin ceasefire talks 'immediately' — but Ukraine rejected Putin's Victory Day pause proposal, insisting on a comprehensive long-term ceasefire. Russia set a wartime record in April 2026 with 6,804 long-range drones and missiles launched — 6,663 drones and 141 missiles, a nightly average of 222 drones. The overnight attack into May 1 included 210 Shahed-type drones; Russian strikes hit four Kharkiv gas stations and a kindergarten in Cherkasy region. Ukraine struck Russia's Orsknefteorgsintez refinery in Orsk (1,500 km) and the Perm region — among the deepest drone strikes of the war. ISW data showed Russia's spring 2026 offensive suffered a net loss of 26 sq miles in April as Ukraine pushed back across the Slovyansk and Kostyantynivka directions. Russian total losses reached approximately 1,331,710 by May 1.
footerNote: Data sourced from UN OHCHR, ISW, CSIS, Ukrainian MoD, US DoD, NATO, IAEA, EU Council, UK MoD, and major news outlets including Reuters, BBC, AP, Al Jazeera, Bloomberg, Kyiv Independent, Euronews, and RBC-Ukraine. Casualty figures are estimates; Russia has never released official figures.
